summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 27.5% YoY to INR 95.21 crore; FY27 outlook raised to INR 202 crore from INR 190.56 crore.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 95.21 crore, up 27.5% YoY, with recurring revenue up 43% to INR 82.97 crore (87% of revenue). PAT grew 32.4% to INR 12.03 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR 4.7 crore as receivables rose to INR 39.5 crore. Management raised FY27 revenue outlook to INR 202 crore, leaving a gap of under INR 8 crore to the INR 210 crore goal. International expansion (US subsidiary registered, Middle East and Singapore go-to-market recalibrated) was triggered.

segments.name: Recurring / annuity
segments.commentary: INR 82.97 crore in H1, up 43% YoY; average MRR INR 13.5 crore vs INR 9.67 crore in H1 FY26. Gross churn annualised 2.6% against a 10% internal ceiling.

segments.name: Projects
segments.commentary: INR 12.24 crore in H1, below a strong H1 FY26 but 51% above H2 FY26. Management described project billing as cyclical.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Financial services is the largest vertical at about 41% of revenue. Top 20 clients are 71% of revenue, down from 73%.

segments.name: AI and cybersecurity
segments.commentary: Contributes about 5% of revenue. Six accelerators are in live production with clients.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue outlook raised to INR 202 crore from INR 190.56 crore; INR 210 crore goal now short by under INR 8 crore.
H2 estimate of INR 107 crore: INR 95.4 crore contracted recurring, INR 1.25 crore new recurring, INR 10.35 crore projects.

Weighted H2 pipeline of about INR 110 crore, including a large cloud migration for an existing NBFC client, a significant cybersecurity opportunity and a large migration for a mid-sized global IT services firm.
Management reiterated full-year PAT ambition of INR 24-25 crore; H1 PAT of INR 12.03 crore is in line with that.
Four H2 priorities: convert pipeline, start US and Middle East operations, reduce debtor days, convert profit into cash.
Billable utilisation at 84%, with a target of 88%.
capex_capacity: H1 capex INR 2.36 crore, mainly AI accelerator build cost; accelerators capitalised as intangible assets and amortised over five years.

Headcount flat at 169 (168 a year earlier); revenue per employee rose to INR 56.56 crore for the half (figure as stated in the call; appears to be an annualised or unit error versus the INR 0.44 crore prior-year figure).
Hiring planned for skill gaps and senior resources and for sales and customer-facing roles in new territories; not expected to scale linearly with revenue.
US subsidiary registered; billing awaits remaining registration steps and intimation to exchanges. Singapore subsidiary already operational with active AWS and Zoho customers.
Delivery is from Indian centres; Bhubaneswar stock used for managed security services.
demand_pricing: Management says AWS has not raised prices on any service in several years and has not seen GPU price increases despite AWS capacity-constraint comments.
AWS consumption margins vary by type: 8-12% typical, 18-20% for large migrations, higher under MAP 2.0 programmes. AI and analytics projects earn more than vanilla compute.
AWS payment terms: Workmates pays AWS in 30 days; customers pay in 45-60 days.
Cloud consumption (third-party cost) rose 72 bps to 66.5% of revenue, which drove the YoY gross margin dip.
Marketplace revenue is very small at present.
No live contract yet with large system integrators or GCCs; discussions ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: How much recurring revenue comes from pass-through AWS consumption, and does it include security and value-added services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AWS consumption is about 83% of the INR 95 crore, with services about 17.5%. Security and AI services are blended across managed services and project buckets.

qa_highlights.question: Has AWS capacity constraints or memory costs affected pricing, discounts, credits or GPU/Bedrock availability?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact so far. Management said AWS has not raised prices and expects higher demand to lift consumption and indirect implementation revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the accelerators' revenue contribution, monetisation and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: AI and cybersecurity are about 5% of revenue. Management cited 8-10 live opportunities for VoxoRA and VerID, and about seven or eight CloudTrustmate customers onboarded. No margin or revenue target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did project revenue fall about 27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Project revenue is cyclical and depends on completions. H1 FY26 included long-running projects that completed then. H1 FY27 billing was about INR 12 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Singapore, US and Middle East subsidiaries start operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Singapore is operational with customers added in H1. US registration is partly complete, with a few steps left before billing. Management did not give a Middle East timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company debt-free and does it plan debt or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt planned. Management is open to complementary acquisitions in AI, cybersecurity and analytics, or partnerships in the US and Middle East. Management said there are no current foreign talks.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow was negative INR 4.7 crore and debtor days remain at 62; collections are the main H2 priority.
Gap of under INR 8 crore to the INR 210 crore goal depends on converting a weighted INR 110 crore pipeline.
Project revenue is lumpy; H1 FY27 projects fell versus the prior-year H1.
Gross margin fell YoY (33.5% vs 34.3%) as cloud pass-through share rose to 66.5%.
International expansion carries early-stage execution risk; Singapore go-to-market was recalibrated with no write-off stated.
Top 20 client concentration at 71% of revenue; AWS dependence (single-hyperscaler focus).
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and recurring-revenue metrics, with specific numbers throughout. More cautious on cash conversion and receivables, and vague on the Middle East timeline, Singapore recalibration and AI accelerator monetisation (no quantified targets).
key_quotes: In May, I said that AI and Cloud are not separate trends. They are the same trend.
Recurring revenue grew 43% year-on-year to INR 82.97 crores and now makes up 87% of our revenue against 77% a year ago.
That is where companies like Workmates will survive and that is where our value proposition is to customers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell to 33.5% from 34.3% a year ago as cloud consumption rose to 66.5% of revenue (+72 bps), and EBITDA margin slipped to 17.3% from 17.7%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Headcount flat at 169 and hiring is for skill gaps and new-territory sales roles, not linear scaling; US subsidiary billing awaits registration steps and Singapore is already operational, so new-market capacity is only partly committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Recurring revenue is up 43% to INR 82.97 crore, MRR reached INR 15.9 crore by September, and H2 needs INR 107 crore against INR 95.4 crore already contracted recurring plus a ~INR 110 crore weighted pipeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H1 capex was only INR 2.36 crore, mainly AI accelerator build, and no new plant or large capex was discussed; the company is debt-free with INR 43.88 crore in cash and liquid investments.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Project revenue is lumpy and fell versus strong H1 FY26, operating cash flow was INR -4.7 crore with debtor days at 62, and the INR 8 crore gap depends on converting a weighted INR 110 crore pipeline.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Six AI accelerators are already live in production and 8-10 VoxoRA and VerID opportunities are open, but no launch dates or revenue targets were given.

rows.label: US subsidiary billing start
rows.why: The US entity is registered and billing awaits the remaining registration steps, with no firm date given; Singapore is already operational with active AWS and Zoho customers.

rows.label: Convert profit into cash / cut debtor days
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was INR -4.7 crore against PAT of INR 12.03 crore, receivables rose to INR 39.5 crore from INR 28.99 crore, and debtor days are 62, so collections are a stated H2 priority.

rows.label: Large cloud migration and cyber deals in H2 pipeline
rows.why: A weighted pipeline of about INR 110 crore includes a large NBFC cloud migration, a significant cybersecurity opportunity and a global IT services migration, but none is yet contracted and there is no live large SI or GCC contract.

tone.note: Management was confident on recurring revenue (+43% YoY), MRR growth and the raised FY27 outlook, but cautious on negative operating cash flow and debtor days, vague on the Middle East timeline and AI accelerator monetisation.
